title: Dative 4: Age (Маше двадцать лет)
description: Russian expresses age with the dative case: 'Маше двадцать лет.' The person whose age is being given goes in the dative.
descriptionRussian: Возраст в русском языке выражается через дательный падеж: 'Маше двадцать лет.'
intro: Russian does not say that you are twenty-five. It says that to you there are twenty-five years, so the person whose age it is goes in the dative and never in the subject slot. If you did the numbers book at A1 you already know the three forms of the word for 'year' and which numbers take which. The only new part is the dative in front.
rules: Russian expresses age with the construction: DATIVE experiencer + number + год / года / лет.
The form 'год' goes with 1 (and 21, 31, etc., except 11). 'Года' goes with 2-4 (and 22-24, 32-34, except 12-14). 'Лет' goes with 5-20 and round numbers like 30, 40, 50.
When the experiencer is named, use the dative form of the noun or pronoun: Маше (fem -а), Антону (masc cons), сыну (masc cons), мне (1st sg pronoun).
examples: Маше двадцать лет. (Masha is 20.) Маша → Маше (dat).
Антону тридцать лет. (Anton is 30.) Антон → Антону (dat).
Брату пять лет. (Brother is 5.) брат → брату (dat).
Сыну десять лет. (Son is 10.) сын → сыну (dat).
Мне двадцать пять лет. (I am 25.) я → мне (dat).
Сестре восемнадцать лет. (Sister is 18.) сестра → сестре (dat).

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 3: which form of 'он' is the dative liker?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 3: нравиться puts the liker in the dative. Он → ему. Today's construction (age) also puts the experiencer in the dative. The dative + experiencer pattern is one of Russian's most useful idioms.

items.hint: Whose age it is: that person goes in which case?
items.explanation: The person whose age is being given goes in the dative. Маша → Маше. Note that the construction has no verb 'to be' in the present tense; the dative + number + лет is enough.

items.hint: Брат is masculine consonant. The age experiencer goes in the dative.
items.explanation: Брат → брату. Same dative ending as in Lessons 1 and 2: masculine consonant + -у. The whole construction Брату тридцать лет means 'Brother is 30.'

items.hint: Сын is masculine consonant. Apply the dative rule.
items.explanation: Сын → сыну. Десять (10) takes лет, the form used with 5-20.

items.hint: Сестра is feminine -а. The age experiencer goes in the dative.
items.explanation: Сестра → сестре. Восемнадцать (18) is in the 11-20 range, all of which take лет (none of them follow the 1 / 2-4 patterns).

items.hint: Антон is masculine consonant. Apply the dative rule.
items.explanation: Антон → Антону. Сорок (40) is a round number ending in 0; round numbers all take лет.

items.hint: Age puts the person in which case?
items.explanation: The age construction puts the experiencer in the dative: Мне двадцать пять лет ('to me are twenty-five years').

items.hint: Same age frame, now with a name. Which dative form?
items.explanation: Ages take the dative experiencer: Антону двадцать шесть лет.

items.hint: Feminine -а names take which dative ending?
items.explanation: Feminine -а names take -е in the dative: Маше девятнадцать лет.

blanks: _____ двадцать пять лет. (I am 25 years old.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The age experiencer is dative, and the dative of я is мне. Russians say 'Мне двадцать пять лет' (literally 'to me twenty-five years').

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena is already twenty-five years old.
errorCorrection.explanation: Russian states age with the dative experiencer: the person whose age is given goes in the dative, so Лене, not Лена. There is no verb 'to be' in the present; 'Лене двадцать пять лет' literally means 'to Lena are twenty-five years'.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My brother is already ten years old.
errorCorrection.explanation: Age uses the dative experiencer, so Брат → Брату: 'Брату уже десять лет'. Брат is the nominative, which would be the subject of a normal sentence ('Брат играет'), but the age construction has no verb and marks the person with the dative. The number десять takes лет (the 5-20 form).

errorCorrection.sentence: В этом году я двадцать три года.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This year I am twenty-three years old.
errorCorrection.explanation: Age puts the experiencer in the dative, so the pronoun is мне (dative of я), not я: 'Мне двадцать три года'. Russian has no verb here; the dative plus the number states the age. With двадцать три, 'year' takes the form года (the 2-4 pattern), but the experiencer stays dative.

minimalPairs.explanation: The age experiencer is dative. Маша → Маше; Russians do not say 'Маша двадцать лет'.
The age experiencer is dative. Сын → сыну. The nominative сын would be a subject of a different construction: 'Сын учится' (The son studies).

year (form depends on the number: 1 → год, 2-4 → года, 5+ → лет)
reviewVocab.example: Один год, два года, пять лет.
